questions.question: Which of these flags is NOT enabled by `"strict": true`?
questions.explanation: noUncheckedIndexedAccess must be enabled separately (recent tsc --init output does so). The others are all members of the strict family.

questions.question: What is the difference between `target` and `lib`?
options: target controls the emitted JavaScript syntax; lib controls which built-in APIs are typed
target controls which APIs are polyfilled; lib controls output syntax
They are aliases for each other
target applies only to Node; lib applies only to browsers
questions.explanation: target decides what syntax the compiler emits and down-levels. lib decides which type declarations, such as DOM or ES2022 APIs, are available. Neither adds polyfills.

questions.question: Why is `// @ts-expect-error` generally preferred over `// @ts-ignore`?
options: It suppresses errors in the whole file
It also fixes the underlying error automatically
@ts-ignore no longer works in recent versions
It becomes an error itself once the line no longer has an error, so stale suppressions are caught
questions.explanation: An unused @ts-expect-error is reported (TS2578), so when the underlying problem is fixed you are told to remove the comment. @ts-ignore stays silently.

questions.question: In TypeScript 7, what happens when you compile a file containing `function f(x) { return x; }` with no tsconfig and no flags?
options: It compiles cleanly because strict is off by default
It reports that parameter x implicitly has an any type, because strict defaults to true
It reports a deprecation warning for missing tsconfig
questions.explanation: Since TypeScript 6.0 (and in 7) strict defaults to true, so noImplicitAny is active even without a config. In 5.x and earlier the same file compiled without errors.
